description: Draw a new character, object or place yourself, free, in the current style's own format, and add it to the person's library: a character or object also joins the shot's cast, a place becomes the shot's place (add_to_shot: false only saves it). Use it for simple things the style doesn't have; for a photo-like picture use generate_picture (paid). No Claude usage or credits are spent: you send the drawing as plain data and Dinoctor checks it (bad fields are dropped; a drawing that fails is refused with the reason). action draw (default) sends the drawing; action describe (read-only) returns the exact format for that kind in the current style (or style), with the look the style wants and an example when it has one: read it before drawing. Formats in short: Pixel = {"name","rows":["..##..",...],"colors":{"#":"#535353"}} (up to 28x28, '.' empty; a character also has "eyes":[[col,row]],"mouth":[col,row], faces right and is at least 20 columns wide); Toon character = {"name","skin","shirt","pants","hair":"tuft|bob|ears|antennae|cap|horns|none","hairColor","snout","tail","wide","tall"}, Toon object = {"name","w","h","shapes":[{"type":"rect|ellipse|poly","x","y","w","h","color","points"}]} (y up is negative, stands on y 0); Voxel = {"name","boxes":[{"at":[x,y,z],"size":[w,h,d],"color"}]} (a character's boxes also have "part":"body|legL|legR|armL|armR", plus "eyes","mouth","faceZ"); other styles have their own format (action describe). Places in every style: {"name","sky","horizon","floor","dark","stars","clouds","orb","items":[{"kind","x","z","size"}]}. Returns the new id. Then use look_at_shot to check it.

action.description: draw (default) sends a drawing; describe returns the format to use.

add_to_shot.description: draw: false only saves it to the library. Default true: a character or object joins the shot's cast, a place becomes the shot's place.

drawing.description: draw: ONE drawing object in the style's format (not an array).

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

size.description: draw, character or object: 1 is normal.

style.description: describe: a style id. Default: the project's style.

x.description: draw, character or object: left to right, about -6 to 6. Empty spaces it automatically.

name: draw
